Article Title: Oil prices ease as Saudi Arabia restores key pipeline, traders remain optimistic on US-Iran talks
Article Text:
Oil prices ease below $100 per barrel

Oil prices slipped below the $100-a-barrel mark on Wednesday as Saudi Arabia began restoring crude supplies through a key pipeline to the Red Sea, while hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough in the US-Iran war added to the ease.WTI crude was trading at $90.10 a barrel, down 42 cents, or 0.46%, while Brent crude stood at $99.09, down 16 cents, or 0.16% around 7:30 am IST.The decline came after Brent closed below $100 a barrel on Tuesday for the first time since September 8. Expectations of improving oil supplies, along with efforts to find a diplomatic solution to the nearly seven-month conflict, put pressure on benchmark crude prices.US President Donald Trump has warned that he could "annihilate" Iran, but also said his envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner had held productive talks with Iranian mediators aimed at ending the war."I think there's a lot of momentum for them to make a deal," Trump said.Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia has restarted operations on its East-West Pipeline to the Red Sea, according to three sources briefed on the matter. The move has been accompanied by signs of an increase in Middle Eastern oil flows.The pipeline had been shut on September 11 after drone attacks, which Saudi Arabia blamed on an Iraqi militia, halted crude loadings at the kingdom's Yanbu port.Since the US-Israeli war on Iran disrupted oil flows from Saudi Arabia and other Gulf producers through the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh has been using the pipeline to reroute around 4 million barrels of crude per day to Yanbu. That volume is equivalent to around 4% of global oil supply.Iraq is also increasing its oil exports. Oil minister Basim Mohammed said on Tuesday that the country was exporting more than 3 million barrels per day and expected exports through Turkey to rise to more than 600,000 bpd.Provisional figures from shiptracking firms Vortexa and Kpler put Iraq's crude exports in August at 2.3 million bpd and 2.17 million bpd, respectively. Both estimates were higher than July levels but remained below the February pre-war levels of 3.7 million bpd and 3.362 million bpd, respectively.Adding to the pressure on oil prices, industry data showed US crude inventories increased by 1.8 million barrels in the week to September 18. Analysts polled by Reuters had expected inventories to decline.As the conflict continues for over 6 months now, oil markets have continued to remain volatile as global supply chains continue to face disruption.
Article Summary: WTI crude was trading at $90.10 a barrel, down 42 cents, or 0.46%, while Brent crude stood at $99.09. The decline came after Brent closed below $100 a barrel on Tuesday for the first time since September 8.

Article Title: Trump buys up to $50,000 of Musk’s SpaceX, sells some a week later
Article Text:
Trump buys up to $50,000 of Musk’s SpaceX, sells some a week later

Trump’s investments in Musk’s companies

Microsoft, Amazon among major July trades

Stocks, ETFs and bonds

Trading activity remains high

US President Donald Trump has continued to bet on Elon Musk’s aerospace giant SpaceX, buying between $15,001 and $50,000 worth of the firm’s shares back in July. The transactions were part of a busy month for Trump’s portfolio, which saw 1,156 purchases and sales disclosed in July.According to a public financial disclosure, Trump made the purchase on July 10 and sold some of the shares a week later, on July 17. The SpaceX trades add to Trump’s investment activity involving Elon Musk’s companies, as he also bought and sold Tesla shares during the period.The combined value of those transactions was between roughly $79 million and $270 million, according to an estimation by CNBC. Of the total amount, purchases totalled at least $43.6 million, while sales amounted to at least $35.6 million.Trump had already reported buying between $15,001 and $50,000 worth of SpaceX shares on June 23. SpaceX went public on June 12 in the largest US IPO on record, with the space, satellite and AI provider valued at $1.77 trillion.SpaceX is a major Pentagon contractor and NASA launch provider. It also owns Musk’s xAI, which has a Pentagon contract worth up to $200 million.Musk was Trump’s biggest financial backer in 2024 and later served as an adviser to his administration.Trump also traded Tesla shares several times. He bought between $100,001 and $250,000 of Tesla on June 15 and between $15,001 and $50,000 the following day. He then sold between $131,004 and $365,000 across four transactions before buying another $100,001 to $250,000 of the automaker’s shares on July 27.Trump’s July trading extended well beyond Musk’s companies, with Microsoft and Amazon among the biggest transactions.On July 20, he sold between $5 million and $25 million worth of shares in each company. Three days later, he bought between $100,001 and $250,000 of Microsoft and between $1,001 and $15,000 of Amazon.The same July 20 filing showed Trump selling between $1 million and $5 million of Oracle and buying between $500,001 and $1 million of Nvidia.He also sold between $250,001 and $500,000 of Northrop Grumman shares that day. The trade took place on the same day Trump signed an executive order tightening supply chain requirements for defence contractors and restricting waivers for certain critical materials sourced from China and other covered countries. The disclosure does not show when the trade took place or who made the investment decision.The July disclosure also shows Trump buying between $1 million and $5 million each of Intuit, Marvell Technology, Salesforce and Church & Dwight. He bought between $250,000 and $500,000 of Axon Enterprises, which works frequently with Immigration and Customs Enforcement.Trump also moved money across exchange-traded funds. On July 8, he bought between $1 million and $5 million each of the State Street SPDR Bloomberg International Treasury Bond ETF, Fidelity MSCI Communication Services Index ETF, Vanguard Short-Term Bond Index Fund ETF and Vanguard Dividend Appreciation Index Fund ETF.On the same day, he sold between $1 million and $5 million each of the iShares US Treasury Bond ETF, State Street Communication Services Select Sector SPDR ETF and iShares International Treasury Bond ETF.Ten-year yields climbed on July 8, led by soaring oil prices, after Trump said at the NATO summit in Turkey that he thought a ceasefire with Iran was over.The filing also showed several large purchases of municipal and other bonds, including between $1 million and $5 million each of two Miami-Dade County, Florida, aviation revenue bonds, a St Louis County, Missouri, school district bond and a Main Street Natural Gas bond.The July disclosure follows another heavy month of trading in June, when Trump reported 1,051 transactions worth between $78.1 million and $263.1 million across stocks, bonds and ETFs.His 2025 annual financial disclosure showed more than 21,000 securities trades across eight accounts holding at least $858 million. That compared with 86 stock transactions disclosed during his first year in office in 2017.The White House has repeatedly said Trump’s portfolio is managed independently and that neither he nor his family has a role in investment decisions.“President Trump’s stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third-party financial institutions,” White House spokesman Davis Ingle said in response to CNBC’s questions about Trump’s latest disclosure.“Neither President Trump nor any member of his family has any ability to direct, influence, or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold.”
Article Summary: Trump bought up to $50,000 of SpaceX shares on July 10. He then sold some of the shares a week later, on July 17. SpaceX went public on June 12 in the largest US IPO on record. Trump also bought and sold Tesla shares during the period. Microsoft and Amazon among the biggest transactions.

Article Text:

Gold price prediction

today:

Gold prices are likely to be choppy as safe haven demand and rising interest rates put opposing pressures, says Vedika Narvekar, Research Analyst - Commodities & Currencies, Anand Rathi Shares and Stock Brokers.

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Gold has had a bit of a rollercoaster this past week. It closed marginally higher at $4,378.63/oz on Friday, and prices have stayed choppy since then. Interestingly, the Fed's rate hike wasn't the real story, but it was oil that kept moving gold around.Midweek, news of Saudi Arabia restoring a key pipeline sent gold spiking as much as 2.8% in a session, but that faded once Fed officials flagged that inflation is broader than just an oil problem.By Tuesday, gold had settled into a $4,340-4,360 range, as fresh US-Iran diplomatic hopes knocked oil down over 10%, easing rate-hike worries almost as fast as they'd built up.Talking about the demand, ETF flows tell a genuinely strong story. Global gold ETFs have now seen inflows for nine straight weeks, with $4.24 billion coming in during the week to September 18 alone, over half from the US. China's demand is even more striking with imports through August already crossing 1,000 tons, beating all of 2025 in eight months, aided by cheaper prices earlier this year and a firmer yuan, while the PBOC bought the most gold since 2023, extending its buying streak to nearly two years.The Indian Gold market has been more cautious. Domestic prices are trading below import parity, with discounts widening sharply from $34/oz in July to $78/oz by mid-September, as old-gold exchange and unofficial supply keep local prices soft. Jewellery demand has cooled after August's rally and pullback left buyers hesitant, though wedding-related buying stayed resilient, with a shift toward lighter-weight pieces.Indian gold ETFs still added 1.6 tonnes in August, inflows up 67% month-on-month, even as new investor sign-ups slowed. Imports fell sharply, down 45% m/m, suggesting local supply is comfortably covering demand.With the Fed decision behind markets, gold lacks one dominant story and is reacting to fast-moving headlines instead. The US-Iran developments and Saudi pipeline progress will keep driving oil, currently the main triggers for gold. More Fed speakers are lined up, and their inflation tone matters. Xi Jinping's US state visit and his September 24 meeting with Trump also bear watching given the implications for risk sentiment and the dollar.Gold remains caught between safe-haven support and rising-rate pressure, likely keeping it choppy rather than trending. ETF inflows, China's record imports, and steady central-bank buying still argue for buying dips, though elevated yields and a firm dollar should cap sharp upside. Expect spot gold in a $4,300-4,420 range this week, with MCX gold between Rs 1,51,900-1,55,800/10gm.
Article Summary: Gold prices likely to be choppy as safe haven demand and rising interest rates put opposing pressures, says Vedika Narvekar, Research Analyst - Commodities & Currencies, Anand Rathi Shares and Stock Brokers. With the Fed decision behind markets, gold lacks one dominant story and is reacting to fast-moving headlines instead.

Article Title: He surrendered tenancy rights for redevelopment and got 2 flats worth Rs 1.38 crore; taxman added it as income, why ITAT Mumbai gave him relief
Article Text:
The two flats provided to him under the PAA were valued at Rs 1.38 crore by the stamp duty authorities. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did the tenant win the case in ITAT Mumbai?

This is the case of a man who surrendered his tenancy rights and got flats from the builder in lieu of that. He was then served an income tax notice for the same. He fought a long battle, and finally won relief from ITAT Mumbai.He was a tenant in Mumbai in a housing society that was slated to undergo redevelopment. He received two flats in the redeveloped building in return for surrendering his tenancy rights.The tribunal ruled that a tax demand under Section 56(2)(x) could not be imposed on the individual merely because he received two flats in exchange for giving up his tenancy rights in the redevelopment project.The man had been a tenant of four shops in a Mumbai housing society. When the society opted for redevelopment, he entered into a permanent alternative agreement (PAA) with the builder.Under the arrangement, the man agreed to surrender his existing tenancy rights. In return, the builder was to provide him with two flats in the redeveloped building as permanent alternate accommodation.The two flats provided to him under the PAA were valued at Rs 1.38 crore by the stamp duty authorities, according to an ET report.The Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) from Parel, however, invoked Section 56(2)(x) and treated the entire stamp duty value of Rs 1.38 crore as "income from other sources" in the tenant’s hands. This resulted in the tenant becoming liable to pay income tax on the amount.Section 56(2)(x) applies where a person receives an asset, including property, without consideration or for inadequate consideration exceeding Rs 50,000, with the resulting amount being taxed under the head "Income from other sources".In this case, the tax notice arose because the Income Tax Department proceeded on the basis that he had received the two flats without consideration. His position, however, was that the flats were provided to him as part of the redevelopment arrangement after he surrendered his existing tenancy rights.The matter subsequently went before the Commissioner of Appeals (CIT(A)), which upheld the addition made by the Assessing Officer. The CIT(A) took the view that, in substance, the tenant had received valuable immovable property in return for extinguishing his tenancy rights.The CIT(Appeals) further held that execution and registration of the redevelopment agreements had resulted in the man acquiring absolute ownership rights in the alternate premises. According to the appellate authority, those rights could not subsequently be changed without his consent.On this basis, the CIT(Appeals) concluded that the property had been received during the relevant assessment year, even though physical possession of the flats had not yet been handed over.The CIT(Appeals) also agreed with the Assessing Officer's decision to apply Section 56(2)(x). It held that the tenant had obtained valuable immovable property without providing adequate monetary consideration and therefore confirmed the addition of Rs 1.38 crore to his income.The man challenged this decision before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) Mumbai. On July 16, 2026, the ITAT ruled in his favour.Mihir Tanna, associate director, S.K Patodia LLP, told ET that the Mumbai ITAT had considered a similar issue in March 2026 in the case of Varun Jaisingh Asher, although the facts were different.Tanna explained that tenancy rights are treated as a capital asset and surrendering such rights amounts to a transfer that is taxable under the capital gains provisions.He said that when a property is allotted under a redevelopment arrangement, the allotment represents the consideration received in return for giving up those tenancy rights.Tanna says: “Therefore, the transaction squarely falls within the ambit of capital gains and cannot be brought to tax under the residuary provisions of Section 56(2)(x)”The tenant’s contention was that he had not actually received the alternate premises because construction of the redevelopment project was still underway and possession had not been given to him.He also maintained that the allotment of the new units could not be treated as a property received without consideration. The permanent alternate accommodation was being provided by the builder in return for the surrender of his valuable tenancy rights.The central question before the Mumbai ITAT was whether Section 56(2)(x) could be applied simply because the redevelopment agreements had been executed and registered during the relevant assessment year, even though construction remained incomplete and Devshichhadva had neither obtained possession nor acquired the right to enjoy the alternate premises.The ITAT Mumbai examined the requirement under Section 56(2)(x) that the taxpayer must "receive" immovable property during the relevant previous year. The tribunal held that the word "receives" could not be given an artificial or notional meaning that would result in taxation merely because a redevelopment agreement had been registered.Before the deeming provision could be applied, the tribunal said, there had to be an actual receipt of the immovable property during the relevant period.The ITAT Mumbai also rejected the view that the transaction involved receipt of property without consideration.The tribunal also referred to its earlier decisions in the cases of Snehalata Heramb Dhayagude, Anil Dattaram Pitale and Amar Narendra Joshi. In those matters, the tribunal had recognised that receiving alternate premises after surrendering existing tenancy or property rights does not amount to receiving immovable property either without consideration or for inadequate consideration.In this case, therefore, two fundamental requirements for applying Section 56(2)(x) were not satisfied.The first was the absence of actual receipt of the immovable property during the relevant previous year. The redevelopment project was still under construction and possession of the alternate premises had not been handed over.The second was that the transaction was not without consideration. The alternate accommodation was being provided in return for Devshichhadva surrendering his tenancy rights, which had value.The tribunal's ruling, however, is limited to the question of whether Section 56(2)(x) could be applied in these circumstances. It does not decide whether the surrender or extinguishment of the tenancy rights could have separate capital-gains tax consequences. That remains a distinct issue.
Article Summary: Man was a tenant in Mumbai in a housing society slated to undergo redevelopment. He received two flats in the redeveloped building in return for surrendering his tenancy rights. He was then served an income tax notice for the same. He fought a long battle, and finally won relief from ITAT Mumbai.

Article Title: Banks to open on Sunday ahead of 3-day nationwide strike: What customers should know
Article Text:
The government said it has taken the proactive steps to safeguard the banking needs of citizens. (AI image)

Also read:

Why are bank unions planning a strike?

NEW DELHI: Banks will remain open on Sunday, September 27, to ensure customers have access to essential banking services ahead of a proposed three-day nationwide strike, the government said on Wednesday.The move comes after the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) called for a nationwide strike from September 28 to 30. With September 26 and 27 falling on a weekend, the strike could otherwise lead to an extended disruption in banking services, the govt said.“In view of the proposed three-day nationwide bank strike called by the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) from September 28 to 30, 2026, coinciding with the preceding weekend holidays of September 26 and 27, the government has taken proactive steps to safeguard the banking needs of citizens,” the finance ministry said in a statement.“In order to ensure that the genuine banking needs of the public are not adversely affected for an extended period, all Public Sector Banks and Regional Rural Banks will function normally on Sunday, the 27th of September, 2026,” the ministry said.“The Department reiterates that the welfare and convenience of bank customers remains the Government's foremost priority. The Government and bank managements have appealed to unions to defer the proposed strike, and have also taken measures to ensure that essential banking services continue un-interrupted,” it added.The Reserve Bank of India has also approved the operation of bank branches, offices, ATM-linked branches and currency chests on September 27.“Permission to operate Bank Branches and Currency Chests on Sunday, September 27, 2026. As requested in the above letter, with a view to ensuring that the genuine banking needs of the public are not adversely affected for an extended period, you have our approval for keeping the branches, offices, ATM link branches and Currency Chests of banks fully operational on Sunday, September 27, 2026," the apex bank said.“The banks may be advised to ensure adherence to relevant legal requirements in this regard. A list of Currency Chests of private sector/foreign banks has been sent to you separately,” it added.The UFBU has said bank operations could be disrupted across the country during the three-day strike from September 28 to 30. Since the strike follows the weekend holidays, customers could potentially face an effective five-day disruption in banking services.The timing is also significant as September 30 marks the half-yearly closing of banks, when reconciliation, provisioning, and treasury and market operations are carried out.The UFBU, which claims to represent around 90% of the banking workforce, has said it will proceed with the strike unless there is concrete progress on its key demand for five-day banking.“Responding to the appeal made by the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Indian Banks' Association (IBA), Bank managements to defer the strike, we informed them that if there is any concrete and positive development towards implementation of our demand for introduction of 5 days banking, UFBU will consider the same,” the UFBU said in a statement following a meeting with the deputy chief labour commissioner.UFBU's other demands include an update and improvement of pension, a uniform dearness allowance formula for all pensioners and an option for employees covered under the National Pension System (NPS) to move to the old pension scheme (OPS). Bank unions under the UFBU had also gone on a nationwide strike on September 11 over their demands.The statement came after a conciliation meeting on Tuesday ended without a resolution. In the absence of such progress, the union said it would be “constrained” to go ahead with the proposed strike on September 28, 29 and 30.
Article Summary: The move comes after the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) called for a nationwide strike from September 28 to 30. With September 26 and 27 falling on a weekend, the strike could otherwise lead to an extended disruption in banking services. The Reserve Bank of India has also approved the operation of bank branches, offices, ATM-linked branches and currency chests.

Article Title: Builder delayed Rs 44.36 lakh flat possession by 18 months and charged Rs 30,000 debris fee; Telangana RERA orders him to pay homebuyer 10.7% interest compensation for delay
Article Text:
The builder assured the homebuyer that the flat would be ready for possession by December 26, 2024. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

What the builder said

Why homebuyer won the case

You pay for a flat which the builder promises possession of on an agreed timeline. He delays possession beyond the grace period. What do you do in such a case?Telangana RERA has granted relief to a homebuyer in one such case, ordering the building to pay interest compensation. It found that the builder had delayed handing over the flat by 18 months and had also levied an additional Rs 30,000 as a debris charge.The Telangana RERA authority concluded that the builder had not fulfilled its obligations under the Agreement of Sale and Section 11(4)(a) of the RERA Act . It also rejected the builder's contention that the delay was caused by Covid-19.A man decided to purchase a flat after seeing an advertisement and checking information available on the builder's website. The flat, which was priced at Rs 44.36 lakh, was allotted to him.An Agreement of Sale was signed. The builder assured the homebuyer that the flat would be ready for possession by December 26, 2024. There was also an extended grace period available up to August 2025.Relying on these commitments, the homebuyer paid Rs 40.32 lakh towards the purchase of the flat. This included amounts that were charged for amenities, parking, EV charging and other allied facilities.The promised possession timelines, however, were repeatedly changed by the builder. The homebuyer said he was not given sufficient clarity about when construction would actually be completed, when the promised amenities would be ready or when the Occupancy Certificate would be obtained.There was also the issue of an additional debris charge of Rs 30,000. The homebuyer said this charge had not been disclosed earlier and did not form part of the agreement.The builder, on the other hand, stated that the project had reached nearly 85% completion. It also said that following discussions with homebuyers, the debris charge had been rationalised to Rs 20,000 per flat.Before the Telangana RERA authority, the homebuyer said the delay had put him under continuing financial pressure. He was having to meet his home loan EMI while simultaneously paying rent. He therefore sought interest compensation from the authority under the provisions of the RERA Act.The builder defended the delay by saying that it was making efforts to complete the project within the revised deadline of December 2026. It cited several difficulties that had affected the construction schedule, including a shortage of labour, Covid-19 and legal issues relating to encroachment.He relied on the force majeure clause and cited the Covid-19 pandemic as a reason for the delay in the project. The builder also told Telangana RERA authority about an FTL encroachment issue involving some blocks in the society,According to the builder, these issues had a wider impact on the project. They led to operational setbacks, labour dispersal, panic among customers and the withdrawal of institutional funding.The builder further told the authority that the Telangana High Court subsequently clarified that construction work could proceed in blocks other than Blocks 8 and 9. It also said that the HMDA later confirmed there was no substantial FTL violation, apart from a minor issue that had already been rectified.The builder extended the construction deadline to December 18, 2026. This meant that possession of the flat would be delayed by more than 18 months from the originally committed timeline.On August 25, 2026, the homebuyer secured relief from Telangana RERA. The authority directed the builder to pay interest compensation at the rate of 10.7% for the delay in handing over possession, according to an ET report.Asha Kiran Sharma, Partner at King Stubb and Kasiva, told ET that the Telangana RERA authority rejected the builder's reliance on Covid-19 and its subsequent consequences as an explanation for the delay.Sharma said the authority's reasoning centred on the timing of the Agreement of Sale. The agreement had been executed in February 2023, considerably after the pandemic had subsided.Therefore, according to the authority's reasoning, the builder had entered into its commitment to deliver possession with knowledge of the circumstances in which the project was being executed.It made it clear that the possession date that has been specified in the Agreement of Sale has to be taken into account.The authority also raised objections to the developer's actions on issues beyond the delay in handing over possession.One such issue was the Rs 30,000 "debris charge" added to the homebuyer's account. Telangana RERA rejected this charge, noting that it was not provided for in the Agreement of Sale and was inconsistent with the developer's statutory obligations under the RERA Act.Additionally, the payment record clearly showed that the homebuyer had paid Rs 40.32 lakh towards the total flat cost of Rs 44.36 lakh. These payments had been made without any default. Even after fulfilling his payment obligations, however, he did not receive possession by the committed date of December 26, 2024. The flat remained undelivered even after the expiry of the grace period.The Telangana RERA authority held that these circumstances amounted to a breach of the builder's contractual and statutory obligations under Section 18 of the RERA Act.The Telangana RERA authority said: “The material on record clearly demonstrates a continued pattern of false assurances despite the Respondent’s (builder’s) knowledge of its inability to adhere to the committed timelines, while the project admittedly remains incomplete beyond the stipulated possession date.”The Telangana RERA authority clarified that the homebuyer can seek compensation for mental agony, financial loss and any assured compensation amounts promised by the builder by filing an application in Form 'N' before the Adjudicating Officer under Section 71 of the RERA Act.The authority also struck down the debris charge imposed by the builder. It found that the charge was not supported by the terms of the Agreement of Sale and was contrary to Sections 11(4)(a), 11(4)(d) and 14 of the RERA Act.Telangana RERA directed that the homebuyer is entitled to interest compensation at the rate of 10.7% per annum.The interest is to be calculated on the amounts already paid by the homebuyer and will apply from June 26, 2025 until the date on which lawful possession of the flat is actually handed over.The authority directed the builder to clear the interest arrears accumulated up to the date of the order within 60 days. If the builder does not make the payment, the interest accruing thereafter will have to be paid every month, on or before the 10th day of the following month, until the homebuyer receives possession of the flat.
Article Summary: The builder assured the homebuyer that the flat would be ready for possession by December 26, 2024. The promised possession timelines, however, were repeatedly changed by the builder. Telangana RERA found that the builder had delayed handing over the flat by 18 months and had also levied an additional Rs 30,000 as a debris charge.

Miquel Sàmper Rodríguez, Minister for Business and Labour, Government of Catalonia, Spain,

A.

A.

Global Location Trends 2025

NEW DELHI: With trade ties on the rise, India and Spain could finally see direct air connectivity. Miquel Sàmper Rodríguez, minister for business and labour, government of Catalonia, Spain, has told TOI “direct air links strengthen not just tourism, but also business, investment, talent and academic exchanges, supporting companies expanding across both markets and deepening India–Catalonia ties. ”Excerpts from a conversation:India is at the heart of Catalonia’s international ambitions. Under our 2026–2030 internationalisation strategy, India is a priority market for Catalan companies’ global growth and for attracting investment to Catalonia. In 2025, Catalan exports to India reached €652 million, more than doubling over the past decade, while imports from India have also continued to expand, with 99 Catalan subsidiaries in India and 67 Indian subsidiaries in Catalonia.We now see an opportunity to deepen this relationship through technology, innovation and investment, particularly in AI, DeepTech, semiconductors, HealthTech, Energy Tech, SpaceTech and advanced manufacturing. Catalonia Trade & Investment’s new Delhi office, alongside our Mumbai presence and 30+ years in India, will strengthen business support and institutional dialogue, helping convert this strong foundation into long-term partnerships.It will provide tailor-made information and end-to-end support for Indian companies establishing in Catalonia, while helping Catalan companies enter and expand in India.India is a strategic market for Catalonia, combining a large economy, skilled talent and a strong technology ecosystem. Under Catalonia’s 2026–2030 internationalisation strategy, India is identified as a priority market for Catalan companies’ global growth and for attracting Indian investment into Catalonia. Our new Catalonia Trade & Investment office in Delhi reflects this importance, strengthening engagement with Indian businesses, investors, government and industry bodies.Connectivity is an important enabler of stronger economic relationships. As business, investment and institutional links between India and Catalonia grow, it is natural that we should also look at how we can make it easier for people to move between our markets.Our discussions will include connectivity, as direct air links can strengthen not just tourism but also business, investment, talent and academic exchanges, supporting companies expanding across both markets and deepening India–Catalonia ties.Success would not simply be measured by the number of meetings we have during the visit. It would be measured by what happens after we return.The opening of Catalonia Trade & Investment’s new Delhi office is particularly significant in this context. It provides a long-term platform from which we can continue the conversations initiated during this visit and expand Catalonia’s engagement with the Indian business and investment community. It is a tangible demonstration that we are committed to the relationship for the long term.We are already seeing examples of the potential. The proposed investment by Barcelona-based technology company Submer in Madhya Pradesh’s semiconductor ecosystem demonstrates how Catalan technology and expertise can contribute to India’s high-tech ambitions.The Catalonia Trade & Investment–NASSCOM Letter of Intent can also provide a framework for taking these conversations forward, encouraging greater collaboration between companies, startups and research institutions.If this visit creates the foundations of these kinds of lasting partnerships, it will be a meaningful success.Barcelona and Catalonia offer Indian companies a strong European base, particularly in technology and innovation. Barcelona ranks 3rd globally and 1st in the EU for attracting AI foreign investment projects, while Catalonia ranks 4th globally and 1st in Europe for digital health foreign investment projects, according to IBM’s. Catalonia’s €334.8 billion economy, strong industrial base and 21.7% share of Spain’s manufacturing-industry sales further strengthen the proposition.Beyond these rankings, companies benefit from an ecosystem of universities, research centres, startups, investors and established industries, supported by global platforms such as Mobile World Congress.
Article Summary: India is a strategic market for Catalonia, combining a large economy, skilled talent and a strong technology ecosystem. In 2025, Catalan exports to India reached €652 million, more than doubling over the past decade. Catalonia Trade & Investment’s new Delhi office, alongside our Mumbai presence and 30+ years in India, will strengthen business support and institutional dialogue.

Article Title: Offer recharge plans with shorter validity: Trai tells telcos
Article Text:
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Trai) Tuesday has asked telecom operators to offer shorter validity special tariff vouchers (STV) for voice and SMS service. (Photo: IANS)

New Delhi: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India ( Trai ) Tuesday has asked telecom operators to offer shorter validity special tariff vouchers (STV) for voice and SMS service, in an effort to have options for users who do not need bundled data.Trai's Telecom Consumer Protection (13th Amendment) Regulation, 2026, says the authority has "observed the limitation in the availability of voice-and SMS-only STVs being offered by telecom service providers, where only a limited number of such STVs, concentrated on longer validities were being offered and making low-income consumers deprived of affordable shorter duration choices."Accordingly, Trai has mandated telcos must come out with "STVs with appropriate reduction in tariff exclusively for Voice and SMS" with validity of upto 30 days and renewable on monthly basis. "...such a tariff framework would sufficiently address consumer needs. This amended regulation will provide low-income consumers with more options, allowing them to recharge according to their requirements and financial capacity. Overall, it will improve choices for consumers preferring not to use STVs bundled with data," Trai says.
Article Summary: Trai's Telecom Consumer Protection (13th Amendment) Regulation, 2026. Trai has mandated telcos must come out with "STVs with appropriate reduction in tariff exclusively for Voice and SMS" with validity of upto 30 days and renewable on monthly basis.

Article Title: HC order weighs on confidence: Fortis investors
Article Text:
Domestic and foreign institutional investors of Fortis Healthcare (Fortis) have expressed concern that the Delhi High Court’s order has created a reputational overhang and weighs on investor confidence. (Photo: Reuters)

NEW DELHI: Domestic and foreign institutional investors of Fortis Healthcare (Fortis) have expressed concern that the Delhi High Court 's order, seeking a forensic audit of transactions involving its former promoters Malvinder and Shivinder Mohan Singh, has created a reputational overhang and weighs on investor confidence.The Aug 31 high court order came in a case arising from Japanese firm Daiichi Sankyo's efforts to enforce its arbitral award against the erstwhile Fortis promoters. Last week, Fortis filed a special leave petition (SLP) in SC, challenging the order.Together, domestic and foreign institutional investors hold 57% shareholding, while retail share is over 11% in the company. "The question for the market is whether a transaction that has cleared the entire approval architecture - board, shareholders, CCI, Sebi, the takeover code, ever becomes settled'', Shriram Subramanian MD and founder of InGovern, a proxy advisory firm, told TOI.In 2018, Malaysia's IHH Healthcare acquired a controlling 31.1% stake in Fortis for approximately Rs 4,000 crore. "Questioning a transaction long cleared by all regulators and seeking its forensic audit after nearly a decade, will open a can of worms,'' he added.IHH is a credible strategic investor, and Fortis, after years of promoter-related turmoil and uncertainty, is now on a more stable footing, investors feel, and prolonged legal proceedings could create uncertainty.While the court has made clear that the forensic audit is a fact-finding exercise and does not, by itself, impose liability, investors said the process could still have wider implications for the company."Capital is mobile and investors have alternatives; prolonged uncertainty can therefore have consequences for the company and its shareholders,'' InGovern said in a note.The acquisition was approved by the board, cleared by the CCI, and completed under the Sebi takeover regulations through an open offer that market regulator itself permitted. Neither IHH nor Fortis was a party to the arbitration, the award or the execution proceedings.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court’s order has created a reputational overhang and weighs on investor confidence. Last week, Fortis filed a special leave petition (SLP) in SC, challenging the order. Together, domestic and foreign institutional investors hold 57% shareholding, while retail share is over 11% in the company.

Article Title: 'Growth prompting world to re-rate India'
Article Text:
Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman addresses the gathering at the 53rd National Management Convention of the All India Management Association (AIMA), in New Delhi. (Photo: ANI)

Professionalisation key to separating ownership from management, says Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman

NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Tuesday said that the Indian economy is expanding close to 8%, while global growth has slowed below 3%, prompting the world to re-rate India.Addressing an AIMA event, she called for not just building bigger Indian companies, but better companies that are competitive, innovative, trusted and resilient to lead India into the future.In her address, FM underlined the need to help startups and MSMEs deal with succession planning, governance, conflict management and delegation, while calling for Indian business models."A large share of India's MSMEs and mid-sized enterprises are family owned. Many have strong products, loyal customers and significant growth potential, but expansion can be held back by unclear roles, succession disputes, informal decision making and disagreements within the family," said Sitharaman.She said the challenge is often not entrepreneurship, but institutionalisation and this can be achieved by overhauling management curricula for today's techno-economic realities. "We need professionalisation: separating ownership from management, defining responsibilities, preparing the next generation, and resolving conflicts before they affect the business itself."Sitharaman highlighted that over the next two decades, the challenge is not simply to keep creating more startups, it is to see how many of them can become large, professionally managed and enduring corporations."AIMA can make these enterprises make the difficult transition from founder-led ventures to institution-led companies - without losing the entrepreneurial energy that created them in the first place," said Sitharaman.She also emphasised that sound corporate governance is not simply a set of external codes to be adopted, as it depends on the standards institutions set for themselves."Businesses must engage constructively with govt and regulators. Legal recourse will always remain available, but every disagreement need not begin as litigation. There is considerable value in engaging early, placing evidence on the table, participating seriously in consultations and working towards solutions before differences become disputes," she noted.She also said Indian industry needs to build institutions that combine scale with durability, higher quality, better governance and deeper technological capabilities.
Article Summary: Nirmala Sitharaman: Indian economy expanding close to 8%, while global growth has slowed below 3%. FM underlined the need to help startups and MSMEs deal with succession planning, governance, conflict management and delegation. She said the challenge is often not entrepreneurship, but institutionalisation.

Article Title: Optiemus to take 51.1% in Nothing's CMF venture
Article Text:
Optiemus Group is set to take an initial 51.1% stake in a proposed joint venture that will turn Nothing’s CMF brand into a standalone, majority Indian-owned company.

New Delhi: Optiemus Group is set to take an initial 51.1% stake in a proposed joint venture that will turn Nothing's CMF brand into a standalone, majority Indian-owned company, the two firms said on Tuesday. Nothing will retain a stake and remain a strategic partner.The transaction is subject to conditions, regulatory approvals and definitive agreements. The companies did not disclose the proposed investment or say when the new entity would begin operations.The plan extends a manufacturing partnership announced in Sept 2025. The companies now want to bring product development and intellectual property creation into India alongside assembly, with CMF designing smartphones here for global markets.Their proposed R&D operation will cover industrial design, mechanical and camera engineering, software, connectivity and components. Intellectual property generated through the programme will be held locally, the companies said. They did not specify how ownership of existing CMF designs or technology would be divided between the new entity and Nothing."Now we want to bring that blueprint to India through CMF, together with Optiemus, and build it here, for the world," Nothing co-founder and CEO Carl Pei said.CMF, launched by Nothing in 2023, sells devices in more than 40 countries. Its India volumes rose 83% in 2025, according to Counterpoint Research.
Article Summary: Optiemus Group is set to take an initial 51.1% stake in a proposed joint venture that will turn Nothing’s CMF brand into a standalone, majority Indian-owned company. The companies did not disclose the proposed investment or say when the new entity would begin operations.

Article Title: Sebi may review expiry-day settlement price mechanism
Article Text:
Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Tuesday said the capital markets regulator intends to address concerns over the settlement price for derivatives on expiry days and other related issues. (Photo: IANS)

NEW DELHI: Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Tuesday said the capital markets regulator intends to address concerns over the settlement price for derivatives on expiry days and other related issues.To address market participants' concerns, Sebi floated a consultation paper earlier this month seeking public comments on the proposed changes to the methodology for determining expiry-day settlement prices of index and single-stock derivatives. The proposals include delinking derivatives' settlement prices from the cash-market closing price, discontinuing live indicative index values during the CAS (Closing Auction Session) and making orders placed beyond the 1% band more binding."Having successfully established the CAS as an important market structure reform, we intend to address concerns in respect of settlement price for derivatives on expiry days and other related issues. A consultation paper has already been issued inviting public comment," Pandey said at the 11th JP Morgan India Conference.The regulator proposed two options for determining the settlement price. Under the first, called Blended VWAP, the settlement price would be based on transactions executed during the last 30 minutes of the Continuous Trading Session (CTS) and the 10-minute CAS.The contribution of each period would be based on its actual traded value, with no fixed weight assigned to either.Under the second option, Sebi proposed continuing with the existing CTS Volume weighted average price (VWAP) methodology, under which only trades executed during the last 30 minutes of CTS would be considered. The regulator said the CTS VWAP could be retained as an interim methodology to provide continuity and allow market participants more time to familiarise themselves with CAS.
Article Summary: Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the capital markets regulator intends to address concerns over the settlement price for derivatives on expiry days. To address market participants' concerns, Sebi floated a consultation paper earlier this month seeking public comments on the proposed changes.

Article Title: Hiremath faces key shareholder vote
Article Text:
Left - Sugandha Hiremath, Right - Baba Kalyani

If Sameer, 52, cannot secure his uncle’s backing, the outcome will hinge on public shareholders, who own 31%. ICICI Prudential Fund and Tata Mutual Fund together hold about 6%.

Promoters hold 68.8% stake in Hikal.

MUMBAI: Sameer Hiremath faces a shareholder vote on Wednesday that will decide whether he becomes Hikal’s chairman for the first time. He is vice-chairman and MD of the company, and a nephew of Baba Kalyani, chairman and MD of Bharat Forge.The vote follows the planned exit of his father, Jai Hiremath, 78, who steps down as chairman next month. It comes amid a bitter feud between the Hiremath and Kalyani branches of the family over assets worth more than Rs 1 lakh crore, with Supreme Court referring the dispute to mediation in July.Sameer’s appointment as CMD requires a simple majority under an ordinary resolution. The Hiremaths hold about 35% of Hikal, the Kalyani camp 34%.Proxy advisers are split, with IiAS and SES backing the appointment and InGovern against it. IiAS cited leadership continuity and Sameer’s three-decade association with Hikal; SES said it saw no major governance concerns. InGovern cited governance and board-independence concerns.IiAS noted that with Jai Hiremath’s exit, Sameer would become the sole executive representative of the Hiremath faction at a time when the wider Kalyani-Hiremath dispute, which also touches Hikal’s shareholding control, remains under mediation.Sugandha Hiremath, 74, Sameer’s mother and Baba’s sister, remains on Hikal’s board in a non-executive capacity. Sameer joined Hikal in Aug 1996 and has served on the board since May 1999. He holds 0.47% of Hikal directly and through Sameer Trust.InGovern acknowledged Sameer’s qualifications, extensive experience and his uninterrupted board attendance, but argued that combining the chairman and MD roles weakens the separation between oversight and management. Hikal, it said, had proposed no counterbalance such as an independent chair.Remote electronic voting closed on Tuesday. Shareholders who did not vote electronically can do so at Wednesday’s AGM, with results expected Thursday.The Hiremaths had taken divergent positions on the Kalyanis’ board reappointments in Hikal. In Dec 2023, they voted against Baba’s reappointment, ending his 31-year tenure on the board in Jan 2024. In Sept 2025, they backed the reappointment of his son, Amit Kalyani, vice-chairman and joint MD of Bharat Forge.
Article Summary: If Sameer, 52, cannot secure his uncle’s backing, the outcome will hinge on public shareholders, who own 31%. ICICI Prudential Fund and Tata Mutual Fund together hold about 6%.Promoters hold 68.8% stake in Hikal. The Hiremaths hold about 35% of Hikal, the Kalyani camp 34%.

Article Title: Andhra Pradesh school holiday today: Schools, Anganwadi centres shut in 6 districts due to heavy rain
Article Text:
Andhra Pradesh school holiday today: Schools shut in 6 districts due to heavy rain

Deep depression to cross Andhra-Odisha coast

Heavy rain expected in several Andhra districts

Schools in six districts of Andhra Pradesh will remain closed today, September 23, due to heavy rainfall and the movement of a deep depression over the Bay of Bengal towards the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha coast.The affected districts are Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Anakapalle.The closure also applies to Anganwadi centres in these districts. Authorities have cancelled employees' leave and deployed disaster-response teams in areas considered vulnerable to heavy rain and flooding.According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the deep depression over the westcentral and adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal was moving westwards at 12 kmph in the six hours up to 5:30 am on Wednesday.The system was located about 70 km east-southeast of Kalingapatnam in Andhra Pradesh. It is expected to move west-northwestwards and cross the North Andhra Pradesh-South Odisha coasts between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur, close to Kalingapatnam, by Wednesday night.The IMD has ruled out the system intensifying into Cyclone Arnab. It is likely to cross the coast as a deep depression.Heavy rainfall is likely in parts of Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalle, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam, Konaseema, Kakinada, West Godavari, East Godavari and Eluru.The Andhra Pradesh government has deployed State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams to deal with the rain and possible flood situation in north coastal parts of the state.Squalls with winds gusting up to 75 kmph are likely along and off the North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts from the morning of September 23 to the evening of September 24.Winds of 45 to 55 kmph, with gusts up to 65 kmph, are also expected along and off the South Andhra Pradesh coast during September 23 and 24.Students and parents in the affected districts are advised to follow the latest instructions issued by their respective district administrations and schools.
Article Summary: Schools in six districts of Andhra Pradesh will remain closed today, September 23. Authorities have cancelled employees' leave and deployed disaster-response teams in areas considered vulnerable to heavy rain and flooding. Deep depression over Bay of Bengal moving westwards at 12 kmph in six hours.

Article Title: UNGA address: Donald Trump touts Venezuela oil deal, says it will drive down energy prices worldwide
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump addresses the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) at the UN Headquarters, in New York, USA

Trump highlights 65 billion barrels of oil

Venezuela deal expected to boost oil production

Trump links Venezuela policy to wider US interests

Trump expects Iran deal after US midterm election

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said the oil deal between the United States and Venezuela will help drive down energy costs around the world, describing it as the "largest oil deal in history" and saying it covers 65 billion barrels of oil.Speaking at the UN General Assembly, Trump said the agreement would benefit both Venezuela and the US, while adding that major global oil companies were entering Venezuela."The biggest oil companies in the world are going in [to Venezuela], and the numbers are absolutely incredible," Trump said.Trump said the US and Venezuela had signed an agreement covering 65 billion barrels of oil, which he said would "benefit both Venezuela and the United States enormously and help drive down the cost of energy all over the world".He also said the two countries together "have more than 60% of the oil in the world".The deal centres on Venezuela's vast oil reserves and efforts to revive its oil industry.Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez has said the agreement aims to increase the country's oil production to 1.5 million barrels per day.The deal covers 17 oil fields with a proven potential of 65 billion barrels, according to Rodriguez's statement cited in the background copy.It could bring $100 billion in investment into Venezuela's oil industry and generate more than $209 billion in taxes for Caracas.The US government and an unnamed private operator in Venezuela have set up a new company with rights to untapped oil fields for 100 years, according to the background information.The US is expected to receive 55% of the new company's effective output through an ownership stake and the right to buy oil at cost. A US official said oil bought by the US would go towards its strategic oil reserves and the military.However, Venezuela's oil infrastructure is in poor condition and would require years and billions of dollars in investment to repair.Trump has said the agreement will help lower gasoline prices in the US. But experts believe Venezuelan oil production was unlikely to increase quickly.Amy Myers Jaffe of New York University said the deal could be helpful in the long run but would not immediately change retail gasoline prices. Kevin Book of ClearView Energy Partners said increasing production would take many years because of the scale of investment required.Trump also highlighted the US military operation in January to arrest then-President Nicolás Maduro."Since that day, hundreds of Venezuelan political prisoners have been freed. They’ve let them out of jails, and we’re working closely with the leaders of Venezuela to forge a much better future for the Venezuelan people," Trump said."Our actions in Venezuela are proof that the United States will no longer permit threats to America to gain a foothold anywhere in the Western Hemisphere," he added.The oil agreement has also faced criticism in Venezuela. Harvard University professor and former Venezuelan planning minister Ricardo Hausmann called it a "shameful deal", while criticising the agreement's legitimacy.In his UN remarks, Trump also said he believed the US would reach a deal with Iran after the November 3 midterm elections."I believe we'll make a deal right after the election because it doesn't make sense for them not to. They're waiting to see how I do in the midterm election," Trump said, according to Reuters.Trump also raised the possibility of either reaching an agreement with Iran or taking military action, saying he had "a big decision to make".
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump said the oil deal between the United States and Venezuela will help drive down energy costs around the world. He said the agreement would benefit both Venezuela and the US, while adding that major global oil companies were entering Venezuela. Trump also said he believed the US would reach a deal with Iran after the November 3 midterm elections.

Article Title: Diesel prices hit records as Iran, Ukraine wars disrupt fuel supplies
Article Text:
A price board at a petrol station in Paris, France (Picture credit: Reuters)

Refinery disruptions deepen global diesel squeeze

Russia's refinery attacks hit diesel exports

US diesel stocks remain below seasonal levels

Asia prices remain near record levels

Few quick options to ease fuel prices

Diesel prices have surged to record levels in Europe and the United States as wars in Iran and Ukraine disrupt supplies from major producers and damage refineries, leaving limited options to prevent further gains.European diesel futures closed at an all-time high last week, having more than doubled from the start of 2026. Supply disruptions have also spread to the Red Sea, where Saudi Arabia loads most of its diesel.In the US, average retail diesel prices crossed $6 a gallon for the first time on record this month. In Asia, benchmark diesel prices have also remained close to record levels amid disruptions to Middle Eastern and Russian supplies.The wars in the Middle East and Ukraine have damaged refineries, while facilities elsewhere have been operating at high levels to make up for lost fuel supplies.US refineries were running at their highest level in eight years in late August, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA)."A key issue is that many refineries around the world are already stretched to capacity," the IEA said in a newsletter on Monday."This leaves few available options to prevent a further tightening of supplies and higher prices in the coming months."Middle East diesel exports fell by half between March and August compared with a year earlier, averaging 800,000 barrels per day, according to shipping data from Kpler. The region supplied nearly 41% of Europe's diesel imports in 2025."Any further disruption to Red Sea flows risks tightening an already stretched global diesel market," Kpler analyst George Shaw said, as cited by Reuters.Shaw added that refining capacity remained a key constraint.Russia, the world's second-largest diesel exporter after the US, banned diesel exports in July after Ukrainian drone attacks reduced refinery production.Russia and Ukraine have continued attacking each other's energy infrastructure despite an announcement by US President Donald Trump last week that they had agreed to stop. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Sunday that he would meet Trump in the coming days.Russia had supplied significant volumes of diesel to countries including Turkey and Brazil before the ban, prompting importers to seek alternative supplies.In Europe, diesel stocks at the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp refining and storage hub were at their lowest level for this time of year on September 10, according to Insights Global.US diesel inventories also remain below normal seasonal levels despite high refinery utilisation. Stocks rose by about 600,000 barrels last week but stood at 96.97 million barrels, nearly 15% below the five-year average for the second week of September.Average US diesel prices reached a record $6.52 per gallon on Monday, according to the AAA Automobile Association.In France, the average diesel price reached a record €2.41 per litre on Sunday, according to an AFP analysis.Asian diesel prices have also risen sharply because of disruptions to Middle Eastern and Russian supplies. The benchmark diesel swaps price had eased from a March record of more than $200 a barrel but remained around $180 a barrel on September 18.Current levels are still about twice their pre-war values.China's diesel exports fell 26% in April-June from a year earlier after the government limited refined-product exports, tightening global supplies.Exports subsequently recovered to around 320,000 barrels per day in August, their highest level in nearly 2.5 years, while domestic stocks declined.The disruptions have created limited short-term options for increasing diesel supplies. Rystad Energy vice-president Janiv Shah said some unused refining capacity existed on paper but that little could be activated quickly and supplied with the appropriate crude.A resumption of oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz would likely be the quickest way to ease prices, Shah said, as it would allow Asian refineries to receive supplies.IEA oil industry and markets division head Toril Bosoni warned that if Gulf supplies remained constrained and commercial inventories continued to fall rapidly, higher prices and further reductions in demand could be needed to close the supply-demand gap.Shah said higher prices could reduce diesel consumption, but the short-term effect would be limited because trucking, agriculture, construction and industry have few immediate alternatives.
Article Summary: European diesel futures closed at an all-time high last week, having more than doubled from the start of 2026. In the US, average retail diesel prices crossed $6 a gallon for the first time on record this month. In Asia, benchmark diesel prices have also remained close to record levels amid disruptions to Middle Eastern and Russian supplies.

Article Title: From Russian oil to Belarusian potash, more hypocrisy from Washington
Article Text:
Trump administration faces flak from critics over Belarus potash deal amid pressure on India over Russian energy

TOI correspondent from Washington:

Critics are calling out the Trump administration for hypocrisy and double standards after MAGA supremo Donald Trump announced a potash (fertiliser) deal on Monday with Belarus, a close ally of Moscow, days after he signed a bill which would punish India if it buys Russian energy.Arising from his spat with Canada, which supplies 85 per cent of US-needed potash, a key farming input, Trump announced with his customary fanfare that Washington is working on a “massive Deal” to purchase potash from Belarus at prices “substantially less” than what Washington currently pays Ottawa, calling it good news for American farmers. The move will affect New Delhi because Belarus is also an established supplier of potash to the Indian agricultural market.The apparent double standard is already drawing flak in diplomatic circles. Evan Feigenbaum, a former administration official and a South Asia analyst, has pointed to the contradiction between Washington’s pressure on India over Russian energy and Trump’s willingness to pursue Belarusian potash and said the appearance of “double standards and apparent hypocrisy” can affect perceptions of the US as a negotiating partner.But as has become normal with many announcements by the MAGA boss, he appears to have jumped the gun on the issue – if he's not posturing – because Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko said there was little or no spare potash available for western markets and his country’s production was already contracted. “Even if we wanted to supply other markets we simply don’t have the volume,” Lukashenko said, according to reports from Minsk.Potash is not quite oil or gas, but in agriculture it has a comparable strategic character. Potassium is one of the three major plant nutrients, alongside nitrogen and phosphorus. It helps regulate water uptake, photosynthesis and enzyme activity and improves crop quality, disease resistance and yields.And the global concentration is striking. Canada, Russia and Belarus are the dominant players in the international potash market. Canada alone accounts for about one-third of global supply and is by far the principal supplier to the US Trump's gambit therefore amounts to using a trade war with one major supplier to seek leverage through another supplier that happens to be aligned with a notional geopolitical adversary who is frequently helped through the backdoor.This is because Belarus is landlocked, and European sanctions have restricted its traditional export routes. So any significant new flow of Belarusian potash to the US would face complicated logistics and could require transit through infrastructure and ports of Russia, the very country Trump is trying to squeeze in an effort to end its war with Ukraine.For New Delhi, the question is not simply whether Trump can secure cheaper potash for American farmers; it is whether Washington – by rearranging the global fertilizer market for its own agricultural survival amid a cratering of ties with Canada – ends up making Indian farmers pay more.India requires roughly 4-5 million tonnes of potash a year and is among the world's largest importers. Although India's supply is now diversified among Canada, Russia, Israel, Jordan and others, Belarus is an important source.
Article Summary: Trump administration faces flak from critics over Belarus potash deal. Comes amid pressure on India over Russian energy and Trump's willingness to pursue Belarusian potash. Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko said there was little or no spare potash available for western markets and his country's production was already contracted.

Article Title: Nasdaq hits record high as AI stocks rally; AMD crosses $1 trillion valuation
Article Text:
(Representative image)

Chipmakers power technology rally

Oil and bond yields provide support

Investors still watch Fed moves

Greenland stocks jump, Bitcoin rises

China-US meeting in focus

Wall Street kicked off the week on a strong note as a rally in technology and AI-linked stocks pushed the Nasdaq to a record closing high.A sharp rise in chip stocks, easing treasury yields and a drop in crude prices helped lift sentiment, while investors also watched developments around the Middle East and upcoming US-China talks.The Nasdaq rose 2.26% to 27,122.09 points, marking its first record-high close since June 2. The S&P 500 gained 1.49% to 7,764.70 points, ending about 0.4% below its August 13 record-high close. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.71% to 52,048.83 points.Semiconductor stocks were at the centre of Monday's gains. Intel jumped 12.2%, while Arm Holdings surged 17%, sending the PHLX semiconductor index 4.3% higher.Advanced Micro Devices gained about 10%, taking its market capitalisation above $1 trillion for the first time.Meta also joined the rally, with its shares climbing 11.4%. The rise came after Wells Fargo increased its price target on the social media company following the recent launch of its Muse AI assistant.The gains came despite safety warnings from leaders of major AI companies a week earlier, which had triggered a global technology selloff.Investors instead pointed to signs that spending on AI continues to expand.A retreat in both oil prices and Treasury yields added to the positive mood.The benchmark US 10-year Treasury yield slipped below the psychologically important 5% mark. Brent crude futures fell below $100 a barrel and touched their lowest level since September 9 before settling at $100.34 per barrel.The decline in oil prices came amid speculation about a possible breakthrough in Middle East talks at a UN meeting this week. Washington and Tehran had exchanged threats over the weekend, but US President Donald Trump said he would be open to meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who is expected to attend the UN General Assembly in New York this week."We've been kind of programmed to follow the price of oil and the yield on the US 10-year, and if you look at those two things today, they've shifted from being headwinds to tailwinds for this market, at least in the near term," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth.The strong session did not remove concerns about interest rates. The US Federal Reserve raised rates last week for the first time in three years as it sought to fight inflation.CME's FedWatch showed traders saw a 50% chance of another rate hike next month. Markets are also due to hear commentary from at least 10 central bank policymakers this week.Valuations remained another point of focus. The S&P 500 traded at just under 19 times expected earnings last Friday, its lowest valuation since 2023, according to LSEG data. AI-related heavyweights have been responsible for much of the recent rise in earnings expectations.Shares of US-listed companies with exposure to Greenland also surged after progress in diplomatic negotiations between the United States and Denmark over Greenland's status.Greenland Mines tripled in value, while Greenland Energy more than doubled.Bitcoin also climbed more than 6%, reaching a more than seven-month high. The move lifted shares of Coinbase and Strategy.Meanwhile, Paramount Skydance dropped almost 3% after a source told Reuters that the company had reached a settlement with California and 11 other states that were suing to block its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros Discovery.Markets are also looking ahead to a Chinese-US summit on Thursday. Discussions could include a possible extension of the trade truce between the two superpowers, the Iran war and regulation of AI.A report said the US had proposed extending the trade truce by six months, while China was seeking a longer extension.Eight of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes ended the session higher. Communication services led the gains, rising 4.16%, followed by information technology, which advanced 2.4%.Within the S&P 500, advancing stocks outnumbered declining ones by a 1.4-to-one ratio.The S&P 500 recorded seven new highs and 29 new lows, while the Nasdaq posted 64 new highs and 127 new lows.Trading activity remained relatively strong, with 16.5 billion shares changing hands on US exchanges. That compared with an average of 16.2 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions.
Article Summary: The Nasdaq rose 2.26% to 27,122.09 points, marking its first record-high close since June 2. The S&P 500 gained 1.49% to 7,764.70 points, ending about 0.4% below its August 13 record high close. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.71% to 52,048.83 points.

Article Title: Red Sea hit, Hormuz choked: How Saudi Arabia has kept its oil exports moving
Article Text:
Saudi Arabia ramps up Gulf oil exports after pipeline attack

Saudi shipments show signs of recovery

Why is Ras Tanura important for Saudi Arabia oil trade

Hormuz traffic remains below normal

Saudi Arabia has ramped up crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz after attacks on its East-West oil pipeline disrupted a key alternative route for the Kingdom’s exports.Saudi Aramco loaded about 14 million barrels of crude on seven very large crude carriers (VLCCs) inside the Mideast Gulf on Sunday, according to TankerTrackers.com data. Satellite images seen by Reuters also appeared to show seven tankers near Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura port on the same day.The pipeline attacks forced Saudi Arabia to shut its East-West oil pipeline on September 13, halting crude loadings at the kingdom's Yanbu oil port on the Red Sea. Since September 16, there have been no visible oil loadings from Yanbu.Following the disruption, Aramco cancelled some crude cargo sales to European clients while increasing sales to Asia of crude loaded at its eastern ports inside the Strait of Hormuz.The rise in Gulf loadings adds to signs of a partial recovery in Saudi crude shipments. In a note cited by Reuters, JP Morgan analysts said Saudi oil was moving through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 2.9 million barrels per day over the previous six days, up from just 700,000 bpd in August.Kpler data showed that 22 tankers, mostly VLCCs, carrying 42 million barrels of crude exited the Strait of Hormuz in the week of September 13.Saudi Arabia and Iraq each accounted for 43% of the volume.Saudi Arabia has also sold about 60 million barrels of crude from its Ras Tanura port inside the Strait of Hormuz for loading through ship-to-ship transfers at Oman's Sohar port this month and next, trade sources told Reuters last week.The increase in shipments came as expectations of higher Saudi supplies weighed on oil prices on Monday, pushing the Brent benchmark below $100 a barrel for the first time since September 9.While Saudi crude shipments have increased, overall traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains sharply lower as tensions in the Gulf continue, with the US and Iran in stalemate.Shipping data showed that 17 commodity vessels transited the strait over the weekend, down from 37 a week earlier.Visible traffic through the strait, which handled a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas before the war, has fallen to a trickle. Middle Eastern producers, however, continue to export oil on tankers travelling with their transponders switched off.Among trackable ships, five vessels exited the strait on Sunday, while two smaller oil tankers entered the Gulf, according to provisional data from analytics firm Kpler.The vessels that exited included the very large crude carrier Pinios, two tankers carrying refined oil products and two empty carriers for bulk goods and gas.At the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at the southern end of the Red Sea, 51 vessels made the crossing, with 33 exiting over the weekend. These included an Aframax-sized tanker carrying about 700,000 barrels of Saudi crude, according to Kpler data.That was down from 57 vessels during the previous weekend.Meanwhile, chaos in the Middle East has continued to disrupt global oil supplies for over six months now, with no peaceful resolution in sight.
Article Summary: Saudi Aramco loaded about 14 million barrels of crude on seven very large crude carriers (VLCCs) inside the Mideast Gulf on Sunday. Satellite images seen by Reuters also appeared to show seven tankers near Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura port on the same day.

Article Title: Oil remains above $100 per barrel as traders await potential US-Iran talks
Article Text:
Oil prices remain above $100 per barrel

Oil prices climbed back above the $100-a-barrel mark as tensions in the Middle East continued to intensify, keeping markets on edge. Brent crude rose 0.51% to $100.80 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) gained 0.43% to $92.77, on Tuesday.The rise, however, was limited as traders weighed signs of possible US-Iran talks against the continuing tensions in the Gulf. Oil prices had fallen recently, so traders who were hoping for a further drop were now cutting those bets as they waited for clearer signs from the diplomatic efforts.The US and Iran traded threats on Sunday, even as US President Donald Trump said that he was open to meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who is expected to travel to New York this week for the UN General Assembly.Meanwhile, Iran has also signalled that it could return to negotiations, with the country conveying conditions to mediators over the weekend for re-engaging in talks, Al Jazeera reported, citing Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei. At the same time, developments elsewhere in the region continued to keep pressure on the oil market.Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said they had carried out attacks on Riyadh and a Saudi Aramco facility in Yanbu.The group has also intensified efforts to cut off Saudi-backed forces from the Red Sea coast.The disruption has also affected the movement of oil through the region. Saudi Aramco has increased exports through the Strait of Hormuz after attacks on its East-West Pipeline forced it to stop some shipments through Yanbu.Tanker tracking data showed that Aramco loaded around 14 million barrels of crude on seven supertankers inside the Gulf on Sunday.As the conflict continues, traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has dropped sharply. Only 12 commodity vessels passed through the waterway over the weekend, compared with 35 during the previous weekend, according to shipping data cited by Reuters.The decline came as tensions between the US and Iran continued for over 6 months now, with the two sides remaining in a stalemate.
Article Summary: Brent crude rose 0.51% to $100.80 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) gained 0.43%. The rise was limited as traders weighed signs of possible US-Iran talks against the continuing tensions in the Gulf.

Article Title: Trump traded more securities than all Congress; backs stock-buying ban for all Congress lawmakers, but not president
Article Text:
The sharp increase in presidential trading has renewed concerns about possible conflicts of interest. (AP file photo)

Republicans' stance

Trump trades and the break-up of other lawmakers' trades

Trump’s investments

Trump’s stand

‘Everybody’s profiting’

Did you know that US President Donald Trump has carried out more securities trades than all members of Congress combined since his return to the White House in January 2025? Interestingly, he supports legislation that would prohibit lawmakers from buying and selling stocks without imposing the same restriction on the president.A majority of Americans support prohibiting lawmakers from trading stocks. President Donald Trump himself backed a ban that would restrict members of Congress but leave him outside its scope.A Bloomberg review of financial disclosures found that Trump or his money managers made nearly 28,700 trades during the 17 months from his second inauguration through the end of June, 2026. In comparison, lawmakers on Capitol Hill reported roughly 22,200 transactions over the same period.The sharp increase in presidential trading has renewed concerns about possible conflicts of interest. The debate has largely focused on whether elected officials could use non-public information when trading, but Kedric Payne of the Campaign Legal Center said that is not the only concern.“Even if they’re not trading the stock on non-public information, they still create the appearance of a conflict of interest because they can still influence the value of the stock through their official duties,” he said.Republicans are also seeking to turn opposition to congressional stock trading into a campaign issue ahead of this fall's closely watched midterm elections.“The American people deserve to know that those they elect to public office actually serve the American people and not their own wallets,” Representative Anna Paulina Luna said during a speech at a two-day Republican convention in Dallas last week.The stock-trading prohibition approved by House Republicans in July applies only to members of Congress, their spouses and dependent children. The president is not covered by the measure. This leaves Trump able to continue trading securities despite having access to a broad range of US intelligence and the ability to affect entire sectors through executive orders or statements on social media.Trump has endorsed the House legislation. In his State of the Union address earlier this year, he urged Congress to approve the measure “without delay” so that lawmakers “cannot corruptly profit from using insider information.”Restrictions on stock trading by lawmakers have attracted support across the political spectrum. An Economist/YouGov poll conducted in May found that three-quarters of US citizens believed members of Congress and other elected officials should not be permitted to trade stocks. A slightly smaller share supported a complete ban.The White House did not comment on whether Trump supports extending a stock-trading ban to the president.
